Miami, Florida
December 8, 1938
Dear Bix:
I found the attached letter in one of my desk
drawers this afternoon and I am thoroughly
ashamed at my laxity in not having returned
it to you sooner.
I scarcely need tell you
that I read it with absorbing interest, espe-
cially since Mr. Peck came within a "red hair"
of being on board the ill fated plane.
Incidentally, I frequently discuss China and
the Chinese with Mr. Sayder who seems deeply
interested in them both, and I wonder, there-
fore, whether you would object to my showing
him such, if any, letters similar to the pres-
ent one that you
may be kind enough to send
me. Mr. Snyder is, of course, entirely dis-
creet, but the thought occurs
to me that it
might be embarrassing to you if my familiarity
with you - however respectful it may be - were
to become known to others in this swell Com-
pany•
Mr. Peck is still in Chungking, and Mrs. Peck
is due in Miami about December 20. I am sure
Mrs. P. joins us in the hope that you and
Mrs. Bixby can get down this way while she
is here.
Very sincerely,
Tom

properties.sfomuseum:description: Typewritten letter from “Tom” [Reynolds] to Harold M. Bixby, dated December 8, 1938 in Miami, Florida; cover letter returning a letter from W. [William] L. Bond to S. [Stokely] W. Morgan, dated August 12, 1938, with a CNAC pilot’s report by Hugh S. Woods; includes description of aerial attack by five Japanese military aircraft, a forced landing, and strafing; includes telegram from [Hugh?] Chen in Hankow [Hankou] to Bond; mentions Mr. Snyder, Mr. and Mrs. Peck, Dr. Sun Fo.
